Criteria for share of profit petroleum from Barmer- Sachore Basin  
*2.    SHRI HARISH RAWAT:  
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:  
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:  
(a)  by when commercial production of oil and natural gas from Barmer-Sachore basin is 
expected; 
(b)  whether Central Government would get "Profit Petroleum" from these fields; 
(c)  if so, by when; 
(d)  whether State Government will also be given a share out of this profit; 
(e)  if so, how much percentage; and 
(f)  if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI MURLI DEORA): 
(a) Commercial production of crude oil from the Blo ck RJ-ON-90/1 in Barmer-Sachore 
basin in the State of Rajasthan is likely to start by first quarter of 2009.  
(b) and (c) Yes, Sir. Government will get share of profit petroleum from these fields. The 
share of profits petroleum will be decided as per t he provisions of the Production Sharing 
Contract (PSC). The Profit Petroleum from the proje ct depends upon various parameters 
such as estimated recoverable reserves, prevalent o il and associated gas prices, level of 
investments made on exploration and development eff orts in the block. Profit share to the 
Government will only be available after recovery of cost made under the project as per the 
provisions of the contract.  
(d) to (f) As per the recommendations of Twelfth Finance Commission, Profit Petroleum 
arising out of the PSCs under New Exploration Licen sing Policy (NELP) are to be shared 
with the concerned States in the ratio of 50:50. Ho wever, this profit sharing will not be 
applicable for RJ-ON-90/1 which is a Pre-NELP block. State Government will get royalty at 
the rate of 20% of crude oil production at well hea d price as well as other taxes and duties 
applicable in the State.

Taxes on Ethanol  
3. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will the Minister of PETROL EUM AND NATURAL 
GAS be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether it is a fact that Andhra Pradesh is one of the leading States in production of 
ethanol in the country; 
(b)  whether it is also a fact that different States are  imposing different Sales Tax and 
Value Added Tax on Ethanol, which is hampering the production of greenfuel in the 
country; 
(o) whether, due to differential tax rates, the price of ethanol per litre in India is more than 
what we are importing;  
(d)  if so, whether any proposal has been submitted to F inance Ministry for levying a 
uniform tax on ethanol; and 
(e)  if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI MURLI DEORA): 
(a) Andhra Pradesh is one of the leading States in production of alcohol in the country. 
Alcohol is used for producing inter alia ethanol (ethyl alocohol). In response to the tender 
floated by Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs), the suppliers offered approx. 80,000 KL per 
annum as against the OMCs' ethanol requirement of 40,000 KL per annum for 5% Ethanol 
Blended Programme in the State.  
(b)  As per Entry 54 of the List-II (State List) of the Seventh Schedule of Constitution of 
India, taxes on sale or purchase of goods in a Stat e is a State subject. The States have the 
power to decide on the nature and rate of tax on sale of ethanol. The States of Bihar, Gujarat, 
Maharashtra and Karnataka are imposing 4% Value Add ed Tax (VAT) on ethanol. Uttar 
Pradesh State is imposing Purchase Tax of Rs. 800/ KL. The States of Andhra Pradesh and 
Tamil Nadu are imposing VAT of 12.5% and 8.5% respe ctively. For other States where 
Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) programme has been implemented, ethanol supplies are mostly 
from Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra and Karnatak a on which 3% Central Sales Tax 
(CST) is levied. However, besides VAT/CST,, other levies such as import/export fee, State 
excise admin fee, etc. are also imposed on ethanol. The levy of taxes/fees by certain States 
has affected the implementation of EBP programme in certain States. 
(c)  The Government has not imported ethanol for EBP Programme so far. 
(d)  and (e) The Department of Food & Public Distribution made a proposal to the Ministry 
of Finance relating to the formulation of policy fo r promotion of ethanol as a bio-fuel on 
their part and to include ethanol in the list of "d eclared goods" (or)" goods of special 
importance" which would serve the objective of levy of Sales Tax/ VAT by States at a rate not 
exceeding 4%. An Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers had been constituted 
to deliberate on matters relating to Sales Tax systems in the States, including the switchover 
to Value Added Taxation based system in place of the earlier sales tax systems. As inclusion 
of ethanol in the list of declared goods would have revenue implications for the States, the 
proposal was forwarded to the Empowered Committee o f State Finance Ministers for 
consideration. Ministry of Finance has indicated that it may not be feasible to carry out any 
amendment in the Central Sales Tax Act 1956, if the same is opposed by the States.

and disaparties among different communities.

Volatility in stock markets  
*10.  SHRI DARA SINGH:  
SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:  
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether the stock markets in the country witnessed the biggest single day drop and 
rise this year resulting in single day drop of 1408 .35 points and investors losing wealth of 
Rs. 6,63,975 crore in January, 2008; 
(b)  if so, what are the reasons behind the volatility in stock markets; 
(c)  whether any review has so far been conducted to analyse the reasons for the said steep 
fall and rise of markets; 
(d)  if so, the details thereof along with steps taken, if any, to contain the extreme swings; 
and 
(e)  if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): (a) Sensex and Nifty 
witnessed a fall of 1408.35 points and 496.5 points respectively on January 21,2008. They 
also witnessed a rise of 1139.92 points and 349.90 points respectively on January 25,2008. 
These are the largest single day movements by way of value of indices. They are, however, 
much lower compared to large movements observed earlier in percentage terms. The loss or 
gain arising from market movement is notional.  
(b) to (e) Volatility is inherent in any market. It  is an outcome of perceptions of the 
investors—domestic and overseas, retail and institu tional—about the economy, the sector 
and the company. This perception is influenced by many factors including the macro-economic 
environment, the growth potential of the economy, p olicy credibility of the government, 
corporate performance, domestic and international events and market sentiments.  
The Government does not try to manage or control volatility. The Government's endeavour 
is to build systems and practices and deepen and br oaden markets which can withstand 
volatility. The Government has put in place systems  and practices to promote a safe, 
transparent and efficient market and to protect market integrity. The systems instituted include

Karnataka State Finance Corporation  
*11. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR: Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased 
to state:  
(a)  whether the State Government of Karnataka has approached the Central Government 
to direct Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) to resume refinance facility 
to Karnataka State Finance Corporation so as to enable it to help the Small and Medium 
Enterprises financially; 
(b)  if so, the action taken thereon; and 
(c)  if not, the reasons for delay and by when necessary action in the matter is likely to be 
taken? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): (a) to (c) The Reserve 
Bank of India (RBI) had issued instructions to Small Industries Development Bank of India 
(SIDBI) on June 1,2007 to stop refinance to State Financial Corportions (SFCs) with negative

of Karnataka State Financial Corporation (KSFC) which had negative net worth, the matter 
was taken up with RBI. After detailed follow up the Government of Karnataka has committed

this commitment, RBI has permitted SIDBI on February 18, 2008 to provide refinance to 
KSFC. Accordingly SIDBI has disbursed Rs. 40 crore to KSFC on 22.02.2008.

*12. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to 
state:  
(a)  whether it is a fact that due to heavy fog, the flights from the Indira Gandhi International 
Airport (IGI), New Delhi, had been long delayed; 
(b)  if so, the details of such delayed flights during the last fortnight and financial loss 
suffered as a result thereof; 
(c)  whether such fog spreads also in airports of European countries and the fog is cleared 
there in time to avoid delay; 
(d)  if so, whether Government has approached such countries to provide such technology 
to India to avoid delay and loss; 
(e)  if so, the details thereof; and 
(f)  if not, the steps expected to be taken to avoid delay in future? 

Written Answers to  [26 FEB. 2008]  Starred Questions 9  
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIA TION (SHRI 
PRAFUL PATEL): (a) and (b) During the last fortnigh t on 6th February, 2008, there was 
heavy fog at IGI Airport which resulted in CAT III operations for about 4 hours i.e. 0610 
IST — 1010 1ST Fourteen (14) flights operated durin g this period and delay was from 7 
minutes to 1 hour 41 minutes. Three departures were  rescheduled. Some airlines do not 
maintain details related to delay due to 'landing restrictions' or late clearance for take off. It 
is, therefore, not possible to compute loss on this count.  
(c) to (e) Fog formation is a natural phenomenon, which occurs world wide due to very 
low temperature near the earth surface, resulting in low visibility conditions affecting smooth 
aircraft operations. No standard and effective technologies are available to disperse the fog. 
However, in order to ensure continuity of operations during fog and low visibility conditions, 
International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) has prescribed use of standard equipments/ 
facilities and procedures such as CAT II/CAT III IL S. Such facilities and procedures are 
used at most of the airports around the world, including India.  
(f) In accordance with ICAO guidelines, Airports Authority of India (AAI) has already 
installed CAT III B ILS at IGI airport, which permi ts operation of aircraft up to Runway 
Visual Range (RVR) of 50 meters which can be used b y airlines with certified pilots. All 
airlines are directed/encouraged to plan their operations with the aircraft and pilots capable 
of operating under such low visibility conditions so as to reduce delays.

the rest of the water goes down in the drain due to various reasons; 
(b)  if so, the details of the scheme of Government to h arvest and utilize this unutilized 
rainwater, State-wise; and 
(c)  the number of schemes including Bharat Nirman Yojana being implemented at present 
to stop the drainage of unutilized rainwater, State-wise? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER RESO URCES (SHRI 
JAY PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) The average annual precipitation is estimated 
as 4000 Billion Cubic Metre (BCM) in the country. After accounting for the natural process of 
evaporation etc., the average annual water availabi lity in the country is assessed as 1869 
BCM. It is estimated that owing to topographic, hyd rological and other constraints, the 
utilizable water is 1123 BCM which comprises of 690  BCM of surface water and 433 
BCM of replenishable ground water resources. Rest of the water could be considered to be 
flowing down to sea.  
(b) and (c) With a view to optimally utilize the available resources, several measures for 
development and management of water resources are u ndertaken by the respective State 
Governments which include creation of storages, res toration of water bodies, rainwater 
harvesting, artificial recharge to ground water and adoption of better management practice 
etc. Storage capacity of about 225 Billion Cubic Metres (BCM) has been created so far. As 
per present assessment, the total estimated storage  capacity of the various projects under 
construction is about 64 BCM. Further, the State Government have identified various other 
schemes for investigation and planning and the estimated storage for such schemes is about 
108 BCM. State Government conceive, plan and implem ent major, medium and minor 
schemes (both surface and ground water) for utilization of water resources. Government of 
India is providing Central assistance to the State Government through various schemes/ 
programmes, such as Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme (AIBP); Command Area 
Development and Water Management (CADWM) Piogramme; National Project for Repair, 
Renovation and Restoration of Water Bodies directly linked to Agriculture etc. The Ministry 
of Water Resources encourages conservation of water including measures such as traditional 
water conservation practice, rainwater harvesting and recharge to ground water and adoption 
of better management practices. Government of India  also launched a Pilot Scheme on 
"National Project for Repair, Renovation and Restoration of Water Bodies directly linked to 
Agriculture" in January, 2005 with an estimated cost of Rs. 300 crore with a view to restore 
and augment storage capacity of water bodies and also to recover their lost irrigation potential. 
Schemes for repair renovation and restoration of water bodies have also been taken up with 
World Bank assistance in the State of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka. Proposal 
from West Bengal and Orissa have also been forwarde d by the Department of Economic 
Affairs to the World Bank.
